A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SINQ research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original perplexity, QA, reasoning, quantization-timing and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds weight/activation diagnostics, inference measurements, method-variant evaluations and further comparisons.

M1.justification: The core dual-scaling, normalization and A-SINQ approach remains. v4 adds a no-overhead variant that shares input scales across appropriate layers and absorbs them into preceding layers, including use before GGUF quantization (Section 2.3.1). This is a bounded procedural extension; several details in the expanded log-space pseudocode were already described in v1.

E1.justification: v4 newly uses Chinese Wikipedia and Python-code activation samples for cross-domain comparisons, plus Gaussian inputs and targets in a single-layer simulation (Figure 2). The principal WikiText2/C4, HellaSwag/PIQA/MMLU and AIME benchmark coverage remains.

E2.justification: v4 adds reported comparisons with CrossQuant (Table 16), QTIP and QuIP# (Table 17), and GGUF Q4_0/Q3_KS baselines (Table 9). QuIP# was already cited in v1 but lacked a reported comparison. These additions substantially broaden the comparator families beyond the retained quantization baselines.

E3.justification: New protocols include W4A8/G128 with context length 2048 for CrossQuant, context length 4096 for codebook comparisons, and gemlite, SGLang and llama.cpp inference measurements with specified batch sizes and workloads. v4 also adds Phi-2/3/4 and additional Llama configurations. These extend the evaluation design; the original headline benchmark settings remain.

E4.justification: v4 adds weight/activation correlation diagnostics, a single-layer Adam simulation, column-scaling kurtosis analysis, weight-versus-activation reconstruction comparisons, AWQ/ASINQ kurtosis analysis and the no-overhead quality tradeoff. Conversely, v1's direct kurtosis-versus-imbalance optimization experiment (Figure 2) and 1D-versus-2D tiling ablation (Figure 4b) are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same ten-run quantization-timing summaries, including the same ± values and distribution plot (v1 Table 7/Figure 5; v4 Table 10/Figure 8). The additions introduce no new seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: All twelve v1 tables retain their numerical results after matching renumbered content. v4 adds substantial new results: Table 5 reports 0.8–1.8% kernel overhead, while Table 9 reports Qwen3-1.7B Q4_0 perplexity of 21.30 for GGUF versus 17.65 with SINQ preprocessing. Further mechanism, Phi and comparator results are added, while the removed optimization and tiling plots remove result entries.

T1.justification: v4 corrects the AWQ objective by removing the duplicated input-vector factor in v1 Equation 5 (v4 Equation 6). The matrix-imbalance definition and dual-scale parameterization remain mathematically equivalent. The new inverse-square-root relationship in Equation 4 is presented as an empirical observation, without a theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds dual scaling and matrix imbalance as a new quantization proxy. v4 makes prediction of input activation magnitudes from weight statistics, enabling calibration-free pseudo-activation-awareness, a central contribution. Its abstract and conclusion also add explicit zero-to-negligible inference-overhead claims, materially expanding the paper's main claims.

C2.justification: v1 interprets imbalance as a better optimization target than kurtosis. v4 develops a different mechanism explanation involving training updates, implicit activation importance and prevention of row-wise outliers, supported by weight-versus-activation reconstruction analyses. It also explains the no-overhead variant's scale-sharing constraints and resulting quality/overhead tradeoff, and acknowledges that calibration still provides additional information.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 makes previously mentioned log-domain accumulation and clipping explicit, adding detailed scale bookkeeping and best-iterate recovery. v4 also documents PyTorch scaling around gemlite and adds supplementary-code and licensing disclosures in Appendix A.2. The existing GitHub access information remains; these are documentation improvements rather than evidence that every underlying implementation changed.

R1.justification: The related-work organization and most comparisons remain. v4 adds citations to CrossQuant, QTIP, Adam, gemlite and SGLang, discusses codebook deployment restrictions, and positions SINQ against the assumption that activation-awareness requires calibration. The Sinkhorn–Knopp reference present in v1 is absent from v4.

P1.justification: v4 substantially rewrites the abstract, contribution list, Section 2.2.1 and conclusion around pseudo-activation-awareness. It also revises the calibration explanation, shortens the tiling discussion and reorganizes the appendices around new reproducibility, diagnostic and deployment sections. This changes the explanatory narrative substantially beyond adding experimental content.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column to a two-column layout with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. New mechanism figures replace v1 Figure 2, additional inference/comparison tables appear, and the tiling-ablation panel disappears. The large-model table moves from the main text (v1 Table 3) to the appendix (v4 Table 13), retaining its results.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens the mechanism explanation and deployment evidence. Unlike v1's quantization timings and algebraic overhead discussion, it measures inference overhead at kernel and end-to-end levels and quantifies the no-overhead variant's quality tradeoff. New weight/activation diagnostics and broader comparisons make the main claims more assessable. These gains outweigh the loss of the direct kurtosis-optimization and tiling ablations, although uncertainty reporting remains limited.
